regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality check is IIP at 6.7% YoY — down from 8.8% prior — with core sector at 5.4% and decelerating. Capacity utilisation breaking 77.4% is the one number that earns optimism: at this threshold, private capex decisions move from 'feasibility' to 'commitment', and IIP capital goods at 16.1% confirms orders are converting to installations. The inversion: PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is a 2-month high, yet manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 from 53.5 — services is carrying the composite, and services-led growth at this stage of the cycle historically compresses GVA-GDP statistical alignment.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% looks manageable until you decompose it: food at 5.52%, core at 3.9% (28th percentile — structurally subdued), and fuel at 22.93% (95th percentile, up 288bps in one month). The gap between benign core and explosive fuel is the trap: fuel feeds into transport costs, which feed into food distribution margins, which feed back into food CPI with a 2-quarter lag — the RBI's revised forecast of 5.1% (up 50bps) is acknowledging this transmission chain, not leading it. WPI at 9.92% is the early warning: producer prices running 550bps above consumer prices means margin compression is being absorbed upstream, and when that buffer exhausts, CPI will catch up.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — with CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) is the structural fault line. NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding pressure is migrating downstream: NBFCs, unable to compete for retail deposits, are drawing on bank credit lines, which compounds the very CD ratio stress they are escaping. The last time India sustained CD ratio above 80% through a rate-cut cycle was FY14 — within 12 months, the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency hikes; today's FX reserve buffer of ~$680bn buys time, but not immunity.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% against CPI at 4.45% yields a real rate of 80bps — thin by any historical standard for an economy with fuel inflation at a decade-high. RBI's inflation forecast revision to 5.1% compresses that real rate to near zero on a forward basis, which is precisely the wrong signal to send when the rupee is at a 89th-percentile 95.24 and the CD ratio is structurally elevated. The policy bind: cutting would widen the CAD and pressure INR; holding compresses capex IRRs at the exact moment capacity utilisation is crossing the private investment threshold. The RBI is not driving with one foot on each pedal — it has removed both feet and is coasting.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps from 75.6% — crossing the critical 77% threshold where survey evidence shows private capex intentions convert to orders is the single most important structural signal this month. IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY confirms the conversion is happening; core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) is the counterweight — cement and steel dispatch, the ground-truth proxies for actual construction activity, are decelerating even as budgeted capex headlines remain intact. The inversion: if fuel inflation at 22.93% feeds into construction input costs, project IRRs deteriorate precisely as utilisation crosses the trigger threshold — private capex could stall at the starting line.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 Cr is a strong print, but at the 71st percentile it is not a record — and the YTD at the 14th percentile suggests base effects and advance filings are doing heavy lifting. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% are the more honest consumption signal: two-wheelers index rural and semi-urban demand, and at 55th percentile they confirm mass-market recovery is real, not just urban affluent. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (26th percentile, down from 5.6%) against vehicle loan growth at 18.8% — consumers are financing durables through secured credit while revolving credit cools, suggesting demand is present but balance-sheet discipline is tightening at the margin.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4%, down only 110bps from 82.5%, remains structurally elevated at 75th percentile. NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% YoY (from 10.6% prior) signals wholesale funding pressure migrating downstream.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and retail deposit franchises — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike if RBI tightens liquidity. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months to prevent a credit crunch.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts (to ease deposit competition) or NBFC stress cycles. The last time CD exceeded 82% was 2022, which led to 18-month NBFC underperformance.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capacity Utilisation Breaks 77% — Capex Cycle Firm","data_text":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6%), IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY, and core sector growth at 5.4% YoY. Composite PMI at 54.6 (83rd percentile, 2-month high) with manufacturing PMI at 52.8 signals sustained order book momentum. India GDP FY estimate at 7.7% (80th percentile) and RBI forecast at 6.7% (76th percentile) confirm medium-term capex visibility.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase exposure to project-linked contractors (EPC, infrastructure). Private capex cycle is self-sustaining; public capex (FY26 budget) will compound growth. Avoid defensive sectors — cyclical upside is 18-24 months out.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation above 77% has historically preceded 12-18 months of sustained capex growth and margin expansion in capital goods. The last similar cycle (2016-2018) saw capex stocks outperform by 40%+ over 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP AUM Surge Signals Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (rising 2 consecutive months: 29,845→31,961→32,297), SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile, rising 2 in a row), and SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile). Critically: SIP AUM growing 40% YoY while SIP accounts growing only 25% YoY — average ticket size rising sharply. DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising 2 in a row) and MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile, rising 2 in a row).","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour — affluent retail (HNI/UHNI) entering via SIPs, not mass retail. Overweight large-cap, quality dividend stocks and financial services. Reduce exposure to micro/small-cap and speculative segments. Expect sustained DII inflows for 6-9 months, but watch for reversal signals (SIP growth deceleration, equity MF outflows).","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile and rising 2 consecutive months has historically preceded 8-12 month equity rallies, but also marked inflection points when ticket size peaked. Monitor SIP growth rate deceleration as early warning.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile — Margin Squeeze Ahead","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up 288bps from 20.05%, 95th percentile), WPI at 9.92% (up 14bps, 67th percentile), and CPI headline at 4.45% (up 7bps, 41st percentile). Brent crude at $98.52/bbl (69th percentile, flat) and WTI at $89.66/bbl (76th percentile, flat). RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% from 4.6%, signalling policy concern.","implication":"Margin compression imminent for refiners, power utilities, and transport operators. Overweight energy stocks (oil majors benefit from higher crude) and underweight consumer discretionary (fuel surcharge pass-through limited). Monitor RBI's next policy stance — if fuel inflation persists above 20%, expect rate pause to extend beyond Q2 FY27, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors (auto, housing).","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded 2-3 quarter margin compression cycles in non-energy sectors. Last occurrence (2021-2022) saw auto and logistics stocks underperform by 25-30% over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Threatens Yen Carry Unwind","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.0% (86th percentile, up 25bps from 0.75%), ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up 25bps from 2.0%), and Fed funds at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile). US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% (90th percentile, down 5bps), signalling flight-to-safety. US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile, up 150bps), but US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down 60bps from 2.1%, 49th percentile) — growth slowing despite PMI strength.","implication":"BOJ tightening is the tail risk. If yen carry trades unwind, expect sharp INR/USD volatility and FII outflows from EM equities. Reduce leverage in India equities; hedge FX exposure. Watch Fed's next move — if US growth continues to decelerate, expect rate cuts by Q3 2026, which would ease global liquidity and support EM. Current positioning assumes Fed pauses; a cut cycle would be a positive surprise.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ rate hikes at 86th percentile have historically preceded 3-6 month EM volatility spikes. The 2023 yen carry unwind saw INR/USD spike 400bps in 2 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening Despite Strong FII Inflows","data_text":"INR/USD at 95.24 (89th percentile, down 47bps from 95.71, strong-negative signal score -78). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile, up from -3,111.9 Cr prior month), yet INR still weakening — suggests structural outflows in debt/derivatives offsetting equity inflows. DXY at 100.56 (51st percentile, flat), indicating US dollar strength is not the primary driver; India-specific factors dominating.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to slow INR depreciation, burning reserves. Monitor RBI's forward guidance on FX intervention — if reserves drop below $600 Bn, expect policy tightening (rate hikes, tighter liquidity). Overweight USD-earning sectors (IT, pharma, BPO). Reduce INR-denominated debt exposure; expect 2-3% further INR weakness over 6 months unless RBI signals reserve adequacy concerns.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness despite strong FII inflows has historically signalled RBI reserve depletion cycles. In 2022-2023, similar dynamics preceded 8% INR depreciation over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stock Proxy","data_text":"Office absorption at 26.9 mn sqft (21st percentile, mild-negative signal), yet Nifty IT flat YoY and office vacancy at 14.5% (42nd percentile, improving). Rent growth in Bengaluru at 100.6 (57th percentile) and Mumbai at 125 (38th percentile, lo) — rents stalling despite absorption. Simultaneously, retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (35th percentile, lo, improving 30-point signal). Home loan disbursements at 259,000 (52nd percentile) and affordability index at 3.5 (19th percentile, lo, but rising 62-point signal).","implication":"GCCs (Global Capability Centers) and non-IT corporates are the real office buyers, not traditional IT services. IT services are consolidating footprints (WFH, automation), so office RE is decoupling from Nifty IT. Overweight commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) on GCC demand, but avoid betting on IT services recovery via office absorption. Residential RE is the real play — affordability improving (rates down to 7.85% from 8.15%), and home loan disbursements rising. Underweight Nifty IT; overweight residential RE and GCC-adjacent office plays.","pct_10y":21,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 21st percentile with stalling rents has historically preceded 12-18 month office RE underperformance relative to residential. The 2020-2021 WFH cycle saw office REITs underperform residential by 35% over 18 months.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

77.4% capacity utilisation — up 180bps and crossing the threshold where survey evidence shows private investment intentions convert to actual orders — is the structural signal that earns this cycle genuine credibility. 7.8% GDP with IIP capital goods at 16.1% and two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY confirms that both investment and mass-market consumption are simultaneously expanding, a combination India has not sustained since FY17. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% YoY is decelerating, and cement dispatch — the ground-truth proxy for construction activity — is not corroborating the budgeted capex headline. Watch whether fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) feeds into construction input costs fast enough to compress project IRRs before the private capex cycle fully ignites.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US GDP SAAR at 1.5% — down 60bps from 2.1% — while US PMI composite hits 56.0 (84th percentile) is the central contradiction in global macro: activity surveys and hard output data are diverging at the widest gap since Q1 2023, and one of them is wrong. BOJ at 1.0% (up 25bps) with US 10Y at 4.96% (90th percentile) tightens the yen carry unwind risk — every 25bps of BOJ normalisation historically forces $40-60bn of repatriation from EM assets, and India's ₹29,631 Cr FII equity inflow is sitting in the crosshairs. Euro Stoxx 50 at a 100th-percentile 6,324 with EZ CPI at 3.3% and ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up 25bps) suggests European equities are pricing a soft landing that the ECB's own rate path is simultaneously denying.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr — a 100th-percentile print, rising for two consecutive months — is the most important domestic liquidity signal: SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (92nd percentile) with SIP AUM growing 40% YoY against account growth of only 25% YoY means average ticket size is rising sharply, confirming affluent capital is entering systematically rather than retail breadth expanding. MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile, rising two consecutive months) provides the structural absorption capacity that prevents FII volatility from becoming market dislocation. The stress point: bank CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY means the funding system is running lean — corporate bond issuance at the 0th percentile signals that capital markets are not yet stepping in to relieve bank balance sheet pressure.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty at 23,329 (75th percentile) with India VIX at 10.998 (6th percentile) is a complacency signal: markets are pricing near-zero tail risk at the exact moment fuel inflation is at a decade-high and the BOJ carry unwind is live. REIT prices tell the real estate story more honestly than launches data — Embassy at ₹369.92 (down from ₹438.97), Mindspace at ₹345.06 (down from ₹505.14), and Brookfield at ₹263.49 (down from ₹339.10) are all pricing office stress that the 26.9 mn sqft absorption headline obscures. Home loan disbursements at ₹2,59,000 Cr (52nd percentile) with average loan rates falling to 7.85% from 8.15% supports housing demand, but affordability index at the 19th percentile and unsold inventory at 6,16,000 units (62nd percentile) cap the upside.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact: first, fuel inflation at 22.93% feeding into WPI at 9.92% — a 550bps producer-consumer price gap that, when it closes, will push CPI through the RBI's revised 5.1% forecast and force a policy response that the CD ratio at 81.4% cannot absorb without NBFC funding stress cascading. Second, BOJ at 1.0% triggering yen carry unwind — India's ₹29,631 Cr FII equity inflow reverses faster than DII at ₹58,502 Cr can absorb if the unwind is disorderly, and INR at 95.24 (89th percentile) has limited buffer. Third, private capex stalling at the threshold: capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the trigger, but construction input cost inflation from fuel prices could compress IRRs before orders convert to disbursements — watch IIP capital goods for September, due in six weeks, as the definitive verdict on whether this cycle is real.

"}
